summary: I confirmed DONE for the composer '#' path. Commit 0c0d9eafc added view "picker". The composer asks for it (ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:158-165), and the server answers from the lean change-request index or a lean gh call, with no checks, comment bodies, mergeable or stacks (sourceControlRpc.ts:275-302). Commit 60633eff3 added the 100-row client superset, so the cache key no longer includes the limit (sourceControlAtoms.ts:262-381). Both full PR and issue lists are now one GraphQL request each, with comments{totalCount} and stacks in the same request (gitHubRepositoryLists.ts:49-58, 153-167). The chip is attached at once from the summary (ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:382-441). All four parts of the proposal landed. The leftovers are small: (1) ContextPickerPopup still reads full rows, and its comment wrongly says it shares rows with the '#' picker. (2) Sending before the background detail arrives triggers a second, non-joined detail RPC, because the send path uses a different client cache. (3) The picker's index rows can show stale titles after an edit. (4) Search fallbacks still use the heavy gh --json comments field sets plus a stack GraphQL.

evidence.note: listChangeRequests payload has view: optional Literals(["picker"]). Older servers ignore it.
listPickerChangeRequests: open and all scopes come from gitWorkflow.indexedChangeRequests. Otherwise provider.listChangeRequests runs with fields "summary" and includeStackSummary:false.
The picker branch runs inside cachedRepositoryList, a 30 s per-repository server cache. Its key includes the picker flag.
GITHUB_PULL_REQUEST_SUMMARY_LIST_JSON_FIELDS has no comments, checks, mergeable or diff stats. The index uses it (pullRequestIndex.ts:75-90).
Non-search full lists use github.listPullRequests: one GraphQL request with stacks inline. fields "summary" takes the lean gh path, and enrich is skipped when includeStackSummary is false.
PULL_REQUEST_ROW_FIELDS uses comments { totalCount }. GITHUB_ISSUE_LIST_QUERY (153-167) does the same for issues, used by GitHubCli.listIssues (1432-1439).
SOURCE_CONTROL_LIST_SUPERSET_LIMIT=100 with sliceToRequestedLimit. The issue key is env|cwd|state. The change-request key is env|cwd|state|involvement|view, with no limit.
summaryContextDetail adds the chip at once with staleAfter=attachedAt (line 422). The detail is fetched in the background through detailCache and replaces the stub. On failure the chip is removed.

Leftover: the paperclip 'Add context' picker requests the open PR list without view "picker", so it gets full rows. The comment on line 17 ('Same rows as the composer # picker') has been false since 0c0d9eafc split the keys. Proposal (a) explicitly named this component.

New defect: the send-time refresh of a stale context uses queryClient.fetchQuery with issueDetailQueryOptions/changeRequestDetailQueryOptions (lib/sourceControlContextRpc.ts:201-234, 370-403). That is a separate client cache from the detailCache (sourceControlAtoms.ts:1136, 1176-1240) used by the background fetch. A send during the roughly 1 s detail window therefore starts a second, non-joined getChangeRequestDetail. The server does not dedupe it (sourceControlRpc.ts:585-604), and the send waits for it.
On fetch failure the original context is kept. If both the background and send-time fetches fail, the stub (body "", comments []) is sent.

Title-only edits (action edit without baseRefName) only call invalidateRepositoryLists (list cache), not the change-request index (60 s TTL, pullRequestIndex.ts:22). The '#' picker re-reads the stale index and can show the old title for up to about 60 s, while full lists show the new one.

Status reads load the 'open' index listing only when the 'all' listing is incomplete (100 or more PRs). In smaller repos the picker's first open read is a cold lean gh call (about 0.6 s, which still meets the finding's target), not the warm hit the commit message implies.

Adjacent path left untouched: searchChangeRequests (ContextPickerPopup's server-search fallback, PR tab search) uses gh pr list --search with GITHUB_PULL_REQUEST_SUMMARY_JSON_FIELDS (comment bodies, statusCheckRollup, mergeable; GitHubCli.ts:109-115, 2958-2971) plus enrichChangeRequestsWithStacks (a second GraphQL). searchIssues also requests comments (GitHubCli.ts:2927-2938).

fixDefects: Minor, low-impact leftovers and defects. (1) ContextPickerPopup.tsx:42-47 still requests full open-PR rows (checks contexts first:100 per PR, labels, assignees, stacks in the GraphQL request) for a list that shows only number and title. Its comment on line 17 says it shares rows with the composer '#' picker, which has been false since 0c0d9eafc. It does share the full superset with the overview, PR page, branch selector and create dialog, so the extra cost appears only on a cold open. (2) chatSendShared.ts:102-135 refreshes stale contexts through the ~/rpc/queryClient cache. The chip's background fetch uses sourceControlAtoms' detailCache instead. A send within the detail window after picking therefore makes a duplicate, non-joined gh pr view or issue view (about 1 s), and the send waits for it. This race was introduced by the chip-first change. (3) If both fetches fail, the empty-body summary stub is sent silently (ChatView.logic.ts:326-333). (4) Picker rows come from the change-request index. Non-lifecycle updates (a title edit) drop only the list cache, so the '#' picker can show a stale title for up to about 60 s. (5) The search fallbacks (searchChangeRequests, searchIssues) still fetch comment bodies, statusCheckRollup and mergeable, and run a second stack GraphQL. This is the same pattern as proposal (c), on paths outside the core '#' flow.
implementationSketch: (1) In apps/web/src/components/chat/ContextPickerPopup.tsx, pass view: "picker" to useSourceControlChangeRequestList and fix the comment on line 17. That makes the popup share the composer's picker key, served from the warm index or a lean gh call. Update ContextPickerPopup.browser.tsx expectations. (2) In apps/web/src/hooks/chatSendShared.ts createSourceControlContextFetcher, call fetchSourceControlIssueDetail / fetchSourceControlChangeRequestDetail from ~/rpc/useSourceControl (the detailCache, which joins in-flight reads) instead of queryClient.fetchQuery(issueDetailQueryOptions / changeRequestDetailQueryOptions). This joins the chip's in-flight background read and removes one of two caches for the same data. Then check whether issueDetailQueryOptions/changeRequestDetailQueryOptions in lib/sourceControlContextRpc.ts still have other users, and fold them onto detailCache if not. Add a unit test: pick, then send immediately, and assert exactly one getChangeRequestDetail call. (3) Optional: in refreshStaleSourceControlContexts, when a refresh fails and ctx.detail.body === '' with an empty comments array (a stub), surface a toast or keep the summary but tag it, rather than sending silently. (4) In apps/server/src/ws/sourceControlRpc.ts refreshLinkedChangeRequest, also invalidate the change-request index for title edits (call a gitWorkflow method that wraps invalidatePullRequestIndex), or in listPickerChangeRequests bypass the index right after invalidateRepositoryLists. Add an rpc test: edit a title, then read the picker list, and assert the new title. In listPickerChangeRequests, also serve 'open' by filtering a complete 'all' listing (expose PullRequestIndexListing.complete through indexedChangeRequests) to skip the extra cold gh call in small repos. (5) In GitHubCli.searchPullRequests/searchIssues, switch to the GraphQL search document already in gitHubRepositoryLists.buildGitHubPullRequestListQuery({search:true}), with comments{totalCount} and stacks inline, or to a lean field set for picker search, and drop enrichChangeRequestsWithStacks in GitHubSourceControlProvider.searchChangeRequests. Cover it with a gitHubRepositoryLists test.
decisionReason: Client and server source-control read paths only. No auth, E2EE, Hub protocol or hosted-lifecycle impact.
correction: The auditor's DONE status holds, but the evidence needs four corrections. (a) The auditor implied the 'open' index is usually warm. Status lookups read 'open' only when the 'all' listing is incomplete (pullRequestIndex.ts:180-187), so in repos with under 100 PRs the picker's first read is a cold lean gh call. (b) The auditor missed that the send-time refresh uses a different client cache (queryClient, not detailCache). A send during the chip's background fetch therefore duplicates the detail RPC. (c) The auditor missed that title edits leave the index stale, so the '#' picker can show old titles for up to about 60 s. (d) The ContextPickerPopup comment claiming it shares rows with the composer picker is now wrong. The search fallbacks still use the heavy field sets.
